paper_name: Direct Tax Laws and International Taxation
author: Rahul kp
topic: Gross Total Income vs Total Income
title: GTI vs Total Income
hook: tax is charged on the lower one!
simple_words: GTI is income before Chapter VI-A deductions. Total Income is what is left after them, and tax is computed on it.

definitions.meaning: Sum of income under the five heads, after clubbing, set-off and carry forward of losses, but before Chapter VI-A deductions.
definitions.note: Exempt income is never in GTI

definitions.meaning: GTI minus the deductions allowed under Chapter VI-A. Tax rates are applied on this figure.

key_points: GTI comes first; Total Income comes after ==Chapter VI-A deductions==
Clubbing of income and set-off of losses are done BEFORE reaching GTI
Exempt income (e.g. agricultural income) is left out of both
!!Chapter VI-A deductions are not allowed from the heads' income before GTI!!, only from GTI

formulas.name: Gross Total Income
formulas.rhs: S + H + B + C + O (after set-off, carry forward, clubbing)
formulas.legend: S = Salary, H = House Property, B = Business or Profession, C = Capital Gains, O = Other Sources

formulas.name: Total Income
formulas.legend: D = deductions allowed under Chapter VI-A, limited to the income available

insight.text: Order matters: five heads, set-off and clubbing give GTI; Chapter VI-A deductions then give Total Income.

memory_trick.mnemonic: Gross is the Garden, Total is the Trimmed
memory_trick.explanation: GTI is the wild, full garden of income. Chapter VI-A deductions trim it. Tax is levied on the trimmed Total Income.

steps: Club income and set off losses
exam_tip: If the question asks for GTI, stop before Chapter VI-A deductions. If it asks for Total Income, deduct them.

doubt.question: Is exempt income part of GTI?
doubt.answer: No. Income exempt under the Act is excluded from computation, so it is not in GTI or Total Income.

mistakes.wrong: Deducting Chapter VI-A items while computing a head's income
mistakes.right: Compute heads first; deduct Chapter VI-A only from GTI.

mistakes.wrong: Reporting GTI as the final figure for tax
mistakes.right: Tax is computed on Total Income, i.e. GTI less Chapter VI-A deductions.
Exempt income is excluded from GTI and Total Income.

mistakes.wrong: Ignoring brought-forward loss set-off before GTI
mistakes.right: Set-off and carry-forward of losses are applied before arriving at GTI.

applicability: Income-tax Act; Finance Act, 2025 basis (no rates used)
reviewer_note: No past-paper list was given. Key point 4 and mistake 4 are worded loosely; check them. Some Chapter VI-A deductions are restricted for special-rate incomes, which this note does not cover.
check_notes: Writer: No past-paper list was given. Key point 4 and mistake 4 are worded loosely; check them. Some Chapter VI-A deductions are restricted for special-rate incomes, which this note does not cover.

Checker 1: Key point 3 / definition 1 note: 'agricultural income is left out of both' is correct for GTI and Total Income, but students may read it as having no tax effect at all. Add: 'Agricultural income is exempt under section 10(1), but for non-corporate assessees it is still taken into account (partial integration) to work out the tax rate on non-agricultural income.'

Checker 1: Formula 2 legend: 'limited to the income available' is vague. Better: 'D = Chapter VI-A deductions. They are limited to GTI and are not allowed against income taxed at special rates, such as STCG under section 111A, LTCG under sections 112/112A and casual income under section 115BB.'

Checker 1: Definition 2 / formula 2: the note does not say that under the default new regime (section 115BAC) most Chapter VI-A deductions are not available. Only a few, such as 80CCD(2), 80CCH and 80JJAA, are allowed. Add a one-line note so students do not deduct 80C or 80D under the default regime.
